subject: Switch economics checklist + legal clauses question
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Anne Park <anne.park@novacorp.com>, NovaCorp Procurement <procurement@novacorp.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Switch economics checklist + legal clauses question

Anne / Procurement team —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. We pulled together a compact proposal and a short checklist to make a parity + migration offer workable for both sides. Attached is a draft quote (nova_quote_v3.pdf) and an implementation checklist (implementation_checklist.xlsx).

Quick highlights:
- Price parity: we can match list for core inference units for the first 12 months if you commit to a pilot conversion and a 12-month minimum seat/run rate.
- Migration credits: we propose a staged credit pool (25% on kickoff, 50% at go-live, 25% at 60-day milestone) to cover engineering lift and egress.
- SLA & liability: we need to keep standard commercial caps but are open to a service-level credit schedule instead of changing the cap language.
- Technical fallback: we offer a compatibility window where we maintain a legacy model variant for 30 days post-migration for confidence.

Two asks from your side to finalize terms:
1) Procurement: any non-negotiable contract language (e.g., data residency or indemnity thresholds)?
2) Ops/security: do you need a specific SOC2/pen-test attestation or any additional evidence before starting the pilot?

If that aligns, we can generate a redlined term sheet and a Statement of Work (SOW) for your legal team. I copied Lauren (commercial lead) and Rishi (pricing) to help with details.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: nova_quote_v3.pdf (proposal), implementation_checklist.xlsx (workback/checklist)

From: Anne Park <anne.park@novacorp.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, NovaCorp Procurement <procurement@novacorp.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Switch economics checklist + legal clauses question

Sergio —

Appreciate the summary and the attachments. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we get too deep:

1) Liability cap: our legal team will push to keep a 3x service credit cap for direct damages. If you are proposing to keep your standard cap, can you confirm the dollar threshold and whether the credit schedule (instead of cap adjustments) would be contractually enforced?

2) Data residency: NovaCorp requires EU residency for a subset of customer PII. We need to know whether the pilot traffic can be pinned to an EU region (we'll provide a list of affected customers).

3) Evidence: procurement would like a current SOC2 report and a summary of your pen-test remediation items. Can you share those or a portal link?

Procurement is available for a sync next week — copying them on timing. For pricing: can you confirm total migration credit amount (not just percentages) so procurement can run the cost model?

Thanks —
Anne Park
Sr. Director, Cloud Operations — NovaCorp
anne.park@novacorp.com
+1 (617) 555-2121

Anne —

Thanks for the quick reply. Below is a tight checklist and concrete numbers we can put in a term sheet to help Procurement model this out (I'll also attach the implementation_checklist.xlsx to the hub link).

Commercial/econ breakdown (to be included in redline):
- Matched unit price: $0.0045 per inference token-equivalent (matched to NovaCorp core tier) — applies to baseline usage up to 10M tokens/month for 12 months.
- Migration credit pool: $90k total (structured as: $22.5k at kickoff, $45k at go-live, $22.5k at 60 days). Credits will be applied to invoices as PRORATED credits over the first three billing cycles after go-live.
- Onboarding support: 40 engineering hours of dedicated onboarding, billed against the credit pool unless additional scope is requested.

Legal and SLA suggestions:
- Liability: propose keeping Redwood standard cap (commercially typical), but include a 3-tiered SLA credit schedule that emulates a 3x damage bucket for availability incidents (effectively providing procurement the same recovery without reopening indemnity language).
- Data residency: we can pin pilot workloads to EU region; for long-term residency, we'd propose a scoped SOW for EU-hosted instances with additional per-region hosting add-on.
- Audit evidence: attaching a secure link to SOC2 report (see related_links). We'll also provide a redacted pen-test attestation.

Operational fallbacks:
- 30-day legacy variant hold for key endpoints.
- Rollback plan and runbook included in implementation_checklist.xlsx.

Next steps: if procurement confirms the credit amount is acceptable, I'll work with Legal to draft a short side-letter that codifies the credit schedule and the SLA-credit substitution for cap movement. Rishi — please confirm the $90k number is workable from a unit economics perspective.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Commercial Strategy — Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Switch economics checklist + legal clauses question

All —

I reviewed Lauren's numbers and the $90k credit pool is acceptable from an economics standpoint for the proposed pilot profile (we model 6-8 weeks to stable traffic). A few operational notes:

- We should lock the matched unit price for 12 months from go-live with an annual CPI floor of 0% / cap of 5% in case of macro volatility.
- For the liability issue, I support the SLA-credit substitution side-letter but Legal will want a clear escalation and measurement window (we recommend 30/60-day contestability window).
- I'll ask Solutions Eng to scope the EU pinning runtime; that should be straightforward but may add a modest infra surcharge if customers require dedicated region hosting.

Next steps: Sergio, I think we can send an updated quote + side-letter draft to Anne and Procurement tomorrow and schedule a joint call with Legal for next Wed. Can you run the DocuSign via HubSpot and cc me?

Rishi Malhotra
Pricing & GTM Strategy — Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
